reviewer.tool: agent image read tool on the captured PNGs listed below; numeric Debug AA/pick/OIT state, the T33 anti-aliasing report and the generated/external capture manifest

observations: The shipped default is a single-sample HDR target plus a depth/coverage-aware spatial edge filter inside the existing resolve. AA on/off changes 0.35-1.1% of the viewport in Studio, Clay and Directional and leaves the background mean delta at 0.0, so it is an edge filter, not a global blur or exposure change.

Sub-pixel horizontal wires change by 3,169 pixels (11.4% of the wire region), the grille by 1,316 pixels and the engraved digits by 1,077 pixels at the generated fixture camera. The digit region keeps 100-103% of the AA-off strong-edge samples in the paired modes; the lettering is still crisp in the images.

Against the 2x box-reduced supersampled reference, every inspected region improves in all three modes: Studio digits 109.85 -> 108.73, grille 47.43 -> 46.39, wires 86.76 -> 85.56, chrome 64.85 -> 64.24, normal detail 59.01 -> 58.32, lens 104.69 -> 103.58 and ground grid 31.33 -> 30.47. Whole-frame MAE is recorded but is not used as the verdict because the 2x reference samples different texture LODs and pixel centres.

The wire/grille/chrome/normal/lens regions show no washout, halo or ghost edge in the on/off images. Chrome keeps its bright specular core and dark reflection; the normal-map panel keeps its high-frequency detail; the clear lens stays dark rather than turning into a pale disk.

Picking is a separate nearest-visible R32_UINT target. Five real scene points picked with AA on and off return identical ids and hit flags, with no averaged/non-integer id; the pick image pairs are byte-comparable at those points.

The full-window capture shows the D3D11On12/Direct2D toolbar and title text outside the scene AA. The toolbar text region is byte-identical between AA on/off (max delta 0, same as capture-to-capture noise).

MASK coverage is checked on the established ao-probe cutout sheet: the hole stays open and the dark/total coverage count differs by less than 1% with AA on/off. The layered-glass fixture uses the bounded OIT algorithm (field 243 = 1) and AA changes only 0.2% of that frame, so the OIT composite is resolved before the edge filter. Both are also covered by the T26/T29/T31/T32 lanes.

Three small orbit steps keep the AA change set at 0.94-1.09% of the viewport; the local text contrast remains above 78% of AA-off. Physical 1080p and 1440p viewport crops, a fractional 1537x901 resize and simulated 96/144/192 DPI all keep AA active and drawable.

Resize, Debug AA-off, and device loss are all reported explicitly: resize keeps mode 1/7 taps, forced off reports mode 0/reason 1, and device loss rebuilds the depth SRV and returns to mode 1. AA adds 0 target bytes; the Debug resolve record time is about 15-28 microseconds. Whole-frame Debug medians varied from +0.056 ms to -16.8 ms across runs because adaptive refresh/settle work dominates; frame time is recorded and not asserted as a release claim.

External Camera lens ring/lettering and black body stay crisp and dark; Car paint/grille/window edges remain readable. The pre-existing Car window/trim speckle is still present and is recorded as an authored defect, not hidden by a global blur.

defects.label: known-defect
defects.where: Car windshield/roof/window seams in Studio and Directional
defects.description: Small bright speckles remain along authored window/trim seams. They also appear with AA off and in earlier tasks; the depth-aware filter deliberately does not turn a texture/trim edge into a full-strength geometric blur.

defects.label: known-limitation
defects.where: whole-frame comparison against the 2x validation reference
defects.description: The 2x reference uses different texture LOD/derivative conditions and pixel centres, so whole-frame MAE can be slightly worse for AA-on even while every inspected edge/detail region improves. The lane therefore uses per-region edge MAE and reports the whole-frame value separately; it is not claimed as a quality target.

defects.label: known-limitation
defects.description: T33 ships no TAA/history/reprojection. Small orbit steps are stable and the specular mip reduction is semantic, but a temporal solution would require complete history invalidation and was deliberately not claimed.

positives: AA is depth/coverage-aware: geometric silhouettes get the meaningful blend, while flat-depth texture detail gets a deliberately small 0.12 cap so engraved lettering keeps its contrast.
The pick target is never sampled or resolved by AA, and the UI overlay is recorded after the resolve.
Inputs respect authored semantics: linear/mipmap slots use bounded 4x anisotropic filtering; authored nearest slots keep the point sampler.
Mip reduction is semantic: linear-light color with coverage-weighted alpha, renormalized normals, GGX-alpha RMS for metallic-roughness, plain linear for AO/factor data.
No extra render target is allocated; the depth SRV shares the resolve heap and is recreated on resize and device loss.

acceptance.acceptedReferencesPromotedBy: not applicable for T33 (no accepted reference promoted)
acceptance.note: Per-mode AA on/off pairs, picking identity, UI equality, cutout/OIT checks and per-region SSAA edge error own the verdicts. External Car/Camera/STL are reviewed qualitatively; the whole-frame SSAA MAE and the temporal-AA limitation are recorded rather than hidden.
